answer: A sybil-resistant economy can anchor each identity to a distinct mailbox via return-mail verification. To join, an agent requests a one-time code mailed to a postal address; only the reader can activate it, and one address can never activate a second. A hundred fakes need a hundred mailboxes, postage and weeks of waiting, while an honest agent pays almost nothing once. Like a vine that climbs only where rooted, or velvet worn thin across too many chairs, cheap duplication fails: each extra identity burns real time and money, and an ember of trust ignites only when the letter arrives.
